messages:
nina: Heads up — CI started failing on Windows runners after we upgraded poetry lockfiles. Error is a hash mismatch when pip downloads our wheel from the internal registry.

nina: Error snippet:
```
ERROR: THESE PACKAGES DO NOT MATCH THE HASHES FROM THE REQUIREMENTS FILE.
The package redwood-inference from https://packages.example.com/.../redwood_inference-0.9.0-py3-none-any.whl (sha256:abcdef...) has different hash than what's in the lockfile (sha256:123456...).
```

rob: is this happening only on Windows or across OSes?

nina: only Windows so far (windows-latest). macos and linux runners pull the same wheel fine.

kevin: likely cause: our registry is rewriting filenames (dash vs underscore) or the CI agent is caching a corrupted wheel. Poetry lock stores hashes for sdist/wheel sources and is platform-agnostic, but if the registry serves a platform-specific build with same name but different content, the hash mismatch shows up on some runners.

rob: can you try `pip download --no-deps redwood-inference==0.9.0 -i https://packages.example.com/simple` on a fresh Windows VM and compare sha256?

nina: did that. sha256 from the downloaded file matches the one in the registry UI (abcdef...). The lockfile expects 123456... which matches the wheel we uploaded during the staging release. Looks like the wheel was rebuilt and replaced but lockfile wasn't regenerated — some repos pin the exact wheel hash in poetry.lock and CI still references the old lock.

kevin: ah, we changed the wheel builder to include the platform tag `py3-none-macosx_11_0_arm64` for macos builds but accidentally reused the same version number `0.9.0` for a patched wheel. Poetry lock captured the original wheel hash. Replacing artifact without bumping version causes this.

ci-bot: CI failed: install step — hash mismatch on windows-latest.

rob: temporary mitigations: 1) clear artifact in registry and re-upload original wheel with the expected hash. 2) regenerate poetry.lock from a clean env and commit, then re-run CI. For Windows runner specifically, we can relax hash checking by installing with `pip install --no-deps --trusted-host packages.example.com` but that's yucky.

nina: we fixed the immediate CI by republishing the original wheel (restored from build artifacts) and re-running. But we should prevent artifact replacement with same version in the future.

kevin: long-term: require builder to always append build metadata (`0.9.0+build123`) for any rebuilds, or enforce immutable artifact uploads in the registry. Also add a check in release pipeline: after wheel upload, regenerate poetry.lock and run an ephemeral install step across OS matrix to ensure hashes match.

rob: can we add a git pre-publish hook or validator in the pipeline to detect version reuse? Patch sounds small.

devx-bot: Created issue #3550: Prevent overwriting release artifacts with same version. Suggested fix: enforce immutability in registry + CI validation step. Milestone: 0.9.1

nina: also adding a short note to onboarding docs: if you see poetry lock hash mismatch, try `poetry lock --no-update` then `poetry install --no-root` or regenerate lockfile if the release changed. Will open a PR with the doc snippet.

kevin: thanks — I'll follow up on the builder change. Also consider adding an assert in our packaging test that wheel filename and recorded platform tags match the expected classifier so we don't accidentally reuse the same wheel for a different platform.

rob: nice catch, nina. saved our Windows e2e runs. :raised_hands:
